rationale: Keil entry and scatter-loading support are replaced by the GCC startup and linker script.
Ghidra created one overlapping umbrella function across smaller valid runtime entries; it is not an independent routine.
Keil runtime entry helpers are toolchain mechanics rather than motor behavior.
Reset and exception entry points are owned by the source vector table.
Keil libc, printf, memory and language-runtime helpers are replaced by GCC/newlib equivalents.
Flash-to-RAM call veneers contain no independent behavior.
Low-Flash board setup, calibration, AES binding and transport integration are represented by source-owned subsystems.
AES-256 CTR XOR helper is represented by the checked-in AES implementation.
AES AddRoundKey helper is represented by the checked-in AES implementation.
Table-driven CRC-32/MPEG-2 helper is represented by the source commissioning frame checksum.
AES-256 block encryption helper is represented by the checked-in AES implementation.
AES-256 key expansion is represented by the checked-in AES implementation.
AES MixColumns helper is represented by the checked-in AES implementation.
AES ShiftRows helper is represented by the checked-in AES implementation.
AES SubBytes helper is represented by the checked-in AES implementation.
Keil floating-point and transcendental helpers are replaced by compiler and libm routines; no board policy lives in this range.
Application orchestration, setup workflows, control derivation and device binding are source-owned.
Single-character decimal digit predicate belongs to the C runtime.
Floating-point special-value wrapper belongs to the Keil math support layer.
AES GF(2^8) multiply helper is represented by the checked-in AES implementation.
Keil double-precision arithmetic and conversion helpers are replaced by GCC/libm.
Flash load image copied to 0x1fff8000 at startup; these bytes are not a second behavior implementation.
Time-critical RAM routines are represented by typed source and the RAM-function linker contract.
Tail veneers only forward calls from relocated code to Flash helpers.
IAR program entry glue is replaced by the GCC startup path.
Reset and exception entry points are owned by the source vector table.
IAR data initialization, unpack and runtime helpers are toolchain mechanics.
HC32 DDL peripheral services, MCAN plumbing and IRQ shells are replaced by checked-in board drivers.
Recovered live debug-port policy is implemented by the authenticated SWD access protocol.
Remaining HC32 clock, Flash, GPIO, UART and support driver routines are source-owned through the board layer.
IAR formatted-output and runtime support are replaced by the source debug writer and GCC runtime.
Address-taken USART1 error callback is represented by the board UART status handling.
Address-taken USART1 receive callback frames bytes and dispatches update and authenticated debug commands.
Boot policy, update state machine, authentication, persistence and handoff are source-owned.
Address-taken formatted-output callback is represented by the blocking board UART transmitter.
AES GF(2^8) multiply helper is represented by the checked-in AES implementation.
The historical one-byte first-run trampoline is intentionally replaced by explicit authenticated records.
RAM-resident erase, program and readback behavior is source-owned and partition-bounded.
RAM tail veneers only forward to Flash/DDL helpers and contain no independent policy.
